name: Emma Donoghue
knownFor: Novelist, playwright and historian of lesbian life; author of Room, Hood and Kissing the Witch.
bio: Emma Donoghue was born in Dublin, the youngest of eight children of the critic Denis Donoghue. She took a first-class degree in English and French at University College Dublin and a PhD in English at Girton College, Cambridge, and moved permanently to Canada in 1998, becoming a Canadian citizen in 2004.

She is a novelist, screenwriter, playwright and literary historian. Her first novel, Stir-Fry (1994), was a coming-of-age story about a young Irish woman discovering her sexuality; her fiction ranges from contemporary stories to historical novels, and she is also the author of a history of British lesbian culture.

works.title: Passions Between Women: British Lesbian Culture 1668–1801

events.text: Published her history Passions Between Women.
Hood won the Stonewall Book Award.
Room was shortlisted for the Man Booker Prize and won the Rogers Writers' Trust Fiction Prize.
Won the Alice B Readers Award, given to living writers whose careers are distinguished by consistently well-written works about lesbians.

relevance: Donoghue is a rare writer who has worked as historian, fiction writer and fairy-tale reteller on women who love women. Kissing the Witch, in particular, retells Cinderella, Snow White and others from the point of view of the women in them.
influence: Room made her a best-selling author internationally, and she was nominated for an Academy Award for adapting it as a screenplay. She has won both the Stonewall Book Award and the Ferro-Grumley Award.
